what: The 9.84M decoder's 1,000-step language-model run at four threads, BCIR (kblock+exp+reduce) against PyTorch 2.13 eager and torch.compile at four intra-op threads (train_comparison.py train --task lm --threads 4 --eval-every 100 --lr-scale 0.25; PyTorch's thread count set by the harness since this record, torch_threads recorded), on one host in one session.
host: 4-vCPU Intel Xeon @ 2.80GHz container (AVX-512; the instance after the 2026-10-16 restart), GCC 13.3, Python 3.11.15 (the declared floor); indicative wall times, no PMU

files.r1-a0ea747-*.json, r2-a0ea747-*.json: the tree before NDT-LANES, NDT-ROPE and NDT-ATTN-5 (a0ea747): round 1 BCIR then eager, round 2 compiled, eager, BCIR
files.r3-742234a-*.json: the tree with them (742234a): BCIR, eager, compiled, BCIR, in that order
files.r4-78cbd29-*.json, r5-78cbd29-*.json: the tree with NDT-BETA and NDT-SCHED-1 (78cbd29), in a later session on the same instance: round 4 BCIR, eager, compiled, BCIR; round 5 eager, BCIR, compiled
files.r6-64bfd62-*.json: the tree with NDT-FUSE and NDT-ATTN-6 (64bfd62), in the session of ../fuse/: BCIR, eager, compiled, BCIR, in that order. The runs started from HEAD 8b4f23d with the slices' sources in the working tree, so each record's environment.commit names 8b4f23d; the trainer's four sources were 64bfd62's byte for byte (r6-64bfd62-sources.sha256), and library_sha256 5bf63b77... is the library they build
files.r6-64bfd62-sources.sha256: the SHA-256 of each trainer source the r6 runs compiled, equal to the blob's in 64bfd62
files.r7-14b5941-*.json: the tree with NDT-ATTN-7 (14b5941), in the session of ../attn7/: BCIR, eager, compiled, BCIR, in that order, every run from the committed tree (environment.commit 14b5941; library_sha256 98793d38... the library both BCIR runs built)
